The remainder of the section is devoted to the proof of theorem 3.4. This proof depends on the use of simplicial techniques, and in particular on variants of the Hurewicz theorem. For the convenience of the reader, the simplicial notions and results that we need are recalled in the appendix (section 6). The first step of the proof is the following general lemma, which is of independent interest. It is well-known to experts, but we do not know any written reference for it. Lemma 3.5. Let A : A

If B = h is a standard projective additive, the composition k[Υ]◦Θ is equal to Υ, hence Θ is an isomorphism in this case. Finite direct sums of standard projective additives are isomorphic to standard projective additives, hence Θ is also an isomorphism if B is a finite direct sum of standard additive projectives. Now the source and the target of Θ, viewed as functors of B preserve filtered colimits of monomorphisms, which implies in turn that Θ is an isomorphism if B is an arbitrary direct sum of standard projective additives.
